claims.text: P7: the golden is rebuilt from the pre-change commit fd7b64c with the fixed capture and equals the committed golden on every key; it now holds a whole-statement M1-M16 baseline for the two-credit Monzo invoice fixture (tests/test_import_monzo.py:136), and v1 reproduces every synthetic case, example, fixture and single line.

dispositions.finding: tests/golden/p7_tools/capture_plugin.py:24 — the golden does not cover M1-M16 for every committed fixture; whole statements were captured only when a test called metrics.compute, so the two-credit Monzo invoice fixture was represented only by single categorisation rows.
dispositions.evidence: Wrote the failing check first: test_p7_golden_covers_every_case now requires a fixture whose lines are exactly the Oakfield INV1042 and Acme INVOICE2210 credits (it failed on the old golden). The capture plugin now also wraps categorise.categorise and records every statement it returns (VAT stagger None), so make_p7_baseline.py gives each whole categorised statement an M1-M16 baseline. The rebuild from fd7b64c gives 43 fixtures, up from 37: the 37 earlier ones are unchanged and in the same order, and six whole statements are new, the Monzo invoice fixture among them (M2 = 5700.0). Four single lines moved out of 'lines' because they are now inside a statement with a full baseline. The golden was recompressed with mtime=0, and both fixture-count floors were raised from 37 to 43.

notes: The general fix covers every statement that pre-change tests categorise as a whole, not only the Monzo one. The other five new whole-statement fixtures were missing for the same reason, in other test files. No production code changed in this attempt; R54 code is as verified in verify-10. Commit d079ca2 on bridgie-task/statement-review/T01.
